title: Normalized finite open external-tensor comparison
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p^a}}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Use a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with its specified canonical exchange and projection transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all morphisms are separated of finite type. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite stages. Fix finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $\bar X\to B$, $\bar Y\to B$ be morphisms and let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$ be open immersions. Put $\bar T=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $T=X\times_BY$, and $u=j\times_Bk:T\hookrightarrow\bar T$, with projections $\bar p,\bar q$ on $\bar T$ and $p,q$ on $T$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, set $D=Lp^*K\otimes^LLq^*L$. The canonical open base-change maps and open projection transformations determine a natural isomorphism
$$e_{j,k}:L\bar p^*j_!K\otimes^LL\bar q^*k_!L\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!D$$
whose restriction along $u$ is the identity of $D$. More precisely, factor $u=j_1k_1$ through $X\times_B\bar Y$. Open base change of $j$, projection formula for $j_1$, open base change of $k$, and projection formula for $k_1$ (using the signed symmetry to put its extension factor first), followed by $j_{1!}k_{1!}\cong u_!$, give this isomorphism. The construction using the opposite factorization through $\bar X\times_BY$ gives the same map. Under a swap of factors, the maps $e_{j,k}$ intertwine the signed external tensor symmetries. For any third open immersion $l:W\hookrightarrow\bar W$ over $B$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$, the two composites built from $e$ on $\bar X\times_B\bar Y\times_B\bar W$ agree after the canonical associators and normalized composition identifications of extension by zero. Both restrict to the identity on $K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M$, where $\boxtimes$ means tensor of the projection pullbacks.
